proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a type \(r\), and write \(V_r=(V_{r1},\ldots,V_{rp})\) for a generic cellular vector with law \(P_{r,\theta_r}\). Its endogenous variables are the labeled count coordinates \(V_{r1},\ldots,V_{rp}\); the treatment is \(V_{r i_X}\), and the two outcomes are \(V_{r i_Y}\) and \(V_{r i_Z}\). The polynomial CPCM is causally sufficient, so there is no latent common cause among these endogenous coordinates.

First distinguish recovery of an observational law from identification of a causal functional. Let \(H(z)=(H_1(z),\ldots,H_J(z))^{\mathsf T}\) denote the observable row-PGF vector. Membership in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\), together with \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\), permits application of \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}frontier}\), which yields
\[
 (G_1(z),\ldots,G_K(z))^{\mathsf T}
 =\mathscr R_M(H)(z)
 =\exp\{M^+\log H(z)\},
 \qquad z\in(0,1]^p, \tag{2}
\]
and PGF coefficient uniqueness identifies every labeled observational law \(P_{r,\theta_r}\). Thus (2) is an equality between an observable recovery functional and component PGFs; it does not define an intervention law.

By \(\mathrm{prop{:}polynomial\text{-}class\text{-}inclusion}\), every recovered polynomial-CPCM component has full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\), is causally sufficient, and belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\). Since \(p\geq3\) implies \(p\geq2\), \(\mathrm{thm{:}cpcm\text{-}graph\text{-}transfer}\) identifies its labeled DAG \(D_r\). This invokes the broad graph result only after its own hypotheses have been verified; the ordered embedding \(\iota\) is not needed for that graph-identification step.

Full support supplies the overlap needed to identify every observational kernel. Indeed, for any parent configuration \(a\in\mathbb N_0^{|\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)|}\), completing the other coordinates by zeros gives one vector in \(\mathbb N_0^p\) having positive \(P_{r,\theta_r}\)-mass. Hence
\[
 P_{r,\theta_r}\!\left(V_{r,\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=a\right)>0. \tag{3}
\]
The identified law and graph therefore determine
\[
 p_{rs,\theta_r}(v_s\mid a)
 =
 \frac{P_{r,\theta_r}(V_{rs}=v_s,
          V_{r,\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=a)}
      {P_{r,\theta_r}(V_{r,\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=a)}. \tag{4}
\]
The denominator is positive by (3); for a root it is the mass of the unique empty configuration, namely one.

We next derive the causal law represented by the truncated product. In the causally sufficient acyclic CPCM, generate the coordinates in a topological order using mutually independent node noises and the identified kernels (4). Under \(\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=x)\), intervention modularity replaces only the assignment for \(V_{r i_X}\) by the constant \(x\in\{1,2\}\). Conditional multiplication in that topological order gives
\[
 P_{r,\theta_r}^{\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=x)}(v_{-i_X})
 =\prod_{s\ne i_X}
 p_{rs,\theta_r}\!\left(v_s\mid
 v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}\right)
 \Big|_{v_{i_X}=x}. \tag{5}
\]
This product is a probability mass function, rather than merely a formal expression. All its terms are nonnegative. Sum successively in reverse topological order over the nonintervened vertices. When a current terminal vertex is summed out, no remaining factor depends on its value, while its own conditional mass function sums to one. Repetition leaves total mass one. This also establishes (5) directly from the structural intervention semantics, rather than defining the causal target to equal an arbitrary observable expression.

It remains to justify the expectations in the contrast. If \(N\mid\lambda\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)\), then for every integer \(\ell\geq0\), direct summation gives
\[
 \mathbb E[(N)_\ell\mid\lambda]
 =\sum_{n=\ell}^{\infty}\frac{n!}{(n-\ell)!}
   e^{-\lambda}\frac{\lambda^n}{n!}
 =\lambda^\ell, \tag{6}
\]
where \((N)_\ell=N(N-1)\cdots(N-\ell+1)\). For every integer \(m\geq0\), the finite identity
\(N^m=\sum_{\ell=0}^{m}S(m,\ell)(N)_\ell\), with \(S(m,\ell)\) the Stirling numbers of the second kind, shows from (6) that \(\mathbb E[N^m\mid\lambda]\) is a finite polynomial in \(\lambda\).

Under either intervention, the coordinate \(V_{r i_X}=x\) has moments of every order. All nonintervened root coordinates have fixed positive Poisson rates and hence have moments of every order by (6). Suppose inductively that every parent of a nonintervened node \(s\) has moments of every order. The positive-polynomial rate assumption and the fixed positive-integer exponent assumption give
\[
 \lambda_{rs,\theta_r}
 =\alpha_{rs}+
 \sum_{k\in\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}
 b_{rsk}V_{rk}^{q_{sk}}. \tag{7}
\]
For \(m\geq1\), writing \(h=1+|\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)|\), convexity yields
\[
 \lambda_{rs,\theta_r}^{m}
 \leq h^{m-1}\!\left(
 \alpha_{rs}^{m}+
 \sum_{k\in\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}
 b_{rsk}^{m}V_{rk}^{m q_{sk}}
 \right). \tag{8}
\]
Every term on the right has finite expectation by the induction hypothesis, including when a parent is the fixed intervention coordinate. Equations (6)--(8) imply that \(V_{rs}\) has moments of every order. Induction along the finite acyclic graph proves in particular that \(V_{r i_Y}\) and \(V_{r i_Z}\) have finite first moments under both interventions.

Finally, every factor on the right of (5) is identified by (4), and its graph indices are identified by \(\mathrm{thm{:}cpcm\text{-}graph\text{-}transfer}\). Therefore summing \((v_{i_Y},v_{i_Z})\) against (5) at \(x=2\) and subtracting the corresponding sum at \(x=1\) yields an observable functional. By (5) and the established integrability, this functional equals
\[
 \bigl(\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}\bigr)
 =\mathbb E_{P_{r,\theta_r}^{\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=2)}}
      [(V_{r i_Y},V_{r i_Z})]
  -\mathbb E_{P_{r,\theta_r}^{\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=1)}}
      [(V_{r i_Y},V_{r i_Z})]. \tag{9}
\]
Applying (9) for every labeled type \(r=1,\ldots,K\) identifies \(\boldsymbol\tau\). The assumptions \(p\geq3\) and the fixed embedding \(\iota\) enter only in selecting the one treatment and two response coordinates in (9); broad CPCM graph recovery is supplied separately by \(\mathrm{thm{:}cpcm\text{-}graph\text{-}transfer}\) under \(p\geq2\).

added_lemmas.statement: For \(p\geq 2\), consider a pooled experiment in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\). If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\) and \(((P_r,D_r))_{r=1}^{K}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\), then the observed pooled-law tuple \(\mathscr A_M((P_r)_{r=1}^{K})\) identifies every labeled component law \(P_r\) and every labeled generating DAG \(D_r\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(H_j(z)=\mathbb E[z^{B_{ji}}]\) be the PGF of composition row \(j\), and write \(H(z)=(H_1(z),\ldots,H_J(z))^{\mathsf T}\). Membership of the experiment in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\), whose defining hypotheses are those used in \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}frontier}\), gives
\[
 \log H(z)=M(\log G_1(z),\ldots,\log G_K(z))^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad z\in(0,1]^p.
\]
Because \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\), the same theorem gives the observable inverse
\[
 (G_1(z),\ldots,G_K(z))^{\mathsf T}
 =\exp\{M^+\log H(z)\}. \tag{1}
\]
PGF coefficient uniqueness, also supplied by \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}frontier}\), therefore identifies each full joint law \(P_r\). The coordinate in (1) indexed by \(r\) is tied to column \(r\) of the fixed known matrix \(M\), so this inversion preserves the type labels rather than identifying the laws only up to permutation.

For each \(r\), membership in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\) states that \(P_r\) is generated by a causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable count-valued CPCM with labeled DAG \(D_r\). The cited \(\mathrm{lem{:}cpcm\text{-}dag\text{-}identification}\), which is Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin's Lemma 11, says that the generating DAG of such a direct joint law is identifiable from that law. Applying it to the already identified \(P_r\), separately for \(r=1,\ldots,K\), identifies every \(D_r\). No ordered three-coordinate embedding, polynomial rate restriction, or intervention premise is used in this argument.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem isolates the direct-law CPCM step from the intervention layer: after full-rank labeled unpooling, Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin's Lemma 11 applies already for \(p\geq2\).
added_lemmas.gap: The published CPCM theorem starts from one directly observed joint law; it does not invert several known-composition aggregate laws or preserve cell-type labels through that inversion.
added_lemmas.consumer: It gives prospective bulk designs a broad labeled-DAG guarantee without imposing Poisson source laws, polynomial rates, or a three-coordinate intervention embedding.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Assume \(p\geq3\), fix the ordered injection \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\), and consider a pooled experiment in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\). If \(((P_{r,\theta_r},D_r,\theta_r))_{r=1}^{K}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), then the pooled-law tuple \(\mathscr A_M((P_{r,\theta_r})_{r=1}^{K})\) identifies the \(\iota\)-indexed intervention-contrast vector \(\boldsymbol\tau=((\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}))_{r=1}^{K}\) through the truncated-factorization functional at \(V_{i_X}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The existing mixed statement makes the broad graph conclusion inherit \(p\geq3\) and the ordered embedding. The graph clause is moved to the stronger load-bearing theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}cpcm\text{-}graph\text{-}transfer}\), proved for \(p\geq2\); narrowing this node to the polynomial-subclass intervention clause reserves the three-coordinate premise solely for the contrast.

proposed.statement: Assume \(p\geq3\), fix the ordered injection \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\), and consider a pooled experiment in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\). If \(((P_{r,\theta_r},D_r,\theta_r))_{r=1}^{K}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), then the pooled-law tuple \(\mathscr A_M((P_{r,\theta_r})_{r=1}^{K})\) identifies the \(\iota\)-indexed intervention-contrast vector \(\boldsymbol\tau=((\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}))_{r=1}^{K}\) through the truncated-factorization functional at \(V_{i_X}\).
proposed.justification: This theorem transfers the recovered polynomial-CPCM law and the separately identified labeled graph to the designated intervention contrasts, with \(p\geq3\) used only to choose one treatment and two distinct response coordinates.
proposed.gap: Neither logarithmic unpooling nor the published direct-law CPCM graph theorem by itself identifies the truncated-factorization contrasts from aggregate wells; full support, causal sufficiency, and finite Poisson-polynomial moments must be connected explicitly.
proposed.consumer: It states the causal-effect output available after broad graph recovery when the prospective assay additionally restricts every type to the certified positive-polynomial Poisson subclass.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the effect-only target to the new \(p\geq2\) graph-transfer theorem and to every structural premise used for support, factorization, and moment finiteness; remove the broad graph clause from the node that retains the three-coordinate assumption.

prose_updates.tldr: Known linearly independent raw-count compositions recover unrestricted labeled type laws for arbitrary \(p\geq1\) by a logarithmic count-PGF inverse, with positive Poisson aliases proving necessity. For \(p\geq2\), any recovered count-valued law in the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM class then has its labeled DAG identified; the three-coordinate condition is not part of graph recovery. Intervention contrasts and validation use the stricter compact positive-polynomial Poisson subclass. For \(p\geq3\), the headline is a finite sound tri-valued certifier: it always terminates, and only a \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) output verifies a rational chart-projection cover together with wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local Jacobian nonsingularity, interiority, PGF-tail, and designated-contrast precision bounds. The finite-grid theorem separately proves existence of some finite rational grid and cover with positive exact margins; it does not certify either prescribed synthetic input. Pointwise sample-split Wald inference is conditional on certification, the capped certified-design frontier is finite, and the three-node base/conditional-refinement benchmark status remains open.

project_justification.gap: Transform inversion, Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin's direct-law CPCM theorem, and validated-numerics methods are established separately. Their CPCM result identifies a graph from a direct count-valued joint law for \(p\geq2\), but it does not recover labeled type laws through known multi-composition pools; existing validated-numerics results do not jointly propagate infinite-support PGF tails through graph exclusion, remote within-graph separation, local chart injectivity, Jacobian regularity, covariance, and intervention precision.
project_justification.niche: Prospective known-composition designs need a proof-producing bridge from aggregate raw-count laws to labeled cellular laws and, already for \(p\geq2\), to the broadest justified graph class, with the \(p\geq3\) embedding reserved for intervention contrasts and with inference confined to a compact certifiable polynomial subclass.
project_justification.fill: The project composes the arbitrary-dimensional rank frontier with published pairwise-identifiable CPCM DAG recovery for \(p\geq2\), proves causal minimality of the strict positive-polynomial benchmark directly from its positive edge coefficients, and supplies for \(p\geq3\) an always-terminating one-sided-sound certifier plus a finite capped design frontier. Relative eventual certification is proved only under explicit strict exact slack and uniform convergence of all numerical controls; no prescribed synthetic input is claimed to meet those premises.

prose_updates.related_work: Shih--Hero is credited for logarithmic transform inversion of independent additive components; the integer-multiplicity multivariate count-PGF recovery map and positive unrestricted converse are derived here. Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin Definitions 9--10 describe the causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM setting, and their Lemma 11 identifies a labeled DAG from a direct joint law. Composing that result with labeled full-rank unpooling gives graph recovery for \(p\geq2\), without any ordered three-coordinate embedding or Poisson source restriction. The positive-polynomial Poisson subclass is shown, edge by edge, to be causally minimal and pairwise identifiable rather than acquiring those properties by definition; only intervention, finite-grid, certificate, and Wald layers use that stricter subclass. Carrasco--Florens and Newey--McFadden supply finite-moment minimum-distance ingredients. Rump, Kearfott, and Berz--Makino motivate validated arithmetic, interval global search, and Taylor enclosures. The new validation step jointly carries analytic Poisson-PGF tails through wrong-graph exclusion, the corrected one-sided remote-subset branch, rational chart covers, Jacobian and covariance checks, and designated causal precision. Its relative eventual-certification theorem is conditional on strict exact slack and convergent controls, not an assertion about the two fixed synthetic runs.
prose_updates.interpretation: Full column rank first identifies each labeled cellular observational law; it does not define a graph or an intervention. For \(p\geq2\), the recovered law identifies a labeled DAG on the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM class. The condition \(p\geq3\) and the fixed ordered embedding \(\iota\) enter only when selecting one treatment and two distinct response coordinates. Those intervention contrasts require the narrower causally sufficient positive-polynomial Poisson subclass, whose full support identifies the kernels in the truncated factorization. The certificate handle enumerates the declared finite design class, records all three statuses, and promotes only \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) inputs to the Pareto comparison. Fixed controls always terminate but can remain undecided. Along a control sequence, eventual certification follows only from the separately stated strict-slack and uniform-convergence hypotheses.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Unrestricted rank recovery and stability apply for arbitrary \(p\geq1\). Labeled-DAG transfer applies for \(p\geq2\) to recovered laws in the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable count-valued CPCM class and imposes neither a Poisson source law nor a three-coordinate embedding. Intervention contrasts, finite-grid construction, certification, and Wald inference are confined to the compact causally sufficient positive-polynomial Poisson subclass and, for the designated contrasts, require \(p\geq3\) and fixed \(\iota\). Certification is always terminating and one-sided sound but may be undecided. Eventual certification is conditional on strict positive exact graph, remote, chart, Jacobian, interiority, algebraic, and precision margins together with uniform numerical convergence; it certifies neither prescribed benchmark by itself. Covariance and Wald claims additionally require normalized strictly positive row fractions and give pointwise, not uniform post-selection, coverage. No claim covers unknown thinning, normalization, composition error, shared-well dependence, hidden types, high-dimensional growth, or biologically calibrated coefficient boxes.

statement_notes.justification: After the separate \(p\geq2\) graph-transfer theorem, this result uses \(p\geq3\) only to transfer an identified polynomial-CPCM law and graph to one treatment and two response contrasts.
statement_notes.gap: The published direct-law CPCM theorem identifies the DAG but neither unpools labeled type laws nor proves that the strict polynomial subclass's support, modular factorization, and moments make the designated contrast functional identifiable.
statement_notes.consumer: It states the intervention-effect output available to a prospective known-composition bulk assay after broad graph recovery, without extending finite-grid, certification, or Wald claims beyond the strict polynomial subclass.
